key_insight: AEAPTMS passivation makes perovskite surface electrostatics more uniform and stable, reducing grain-boundary barriers and improving photovoltage dynamics.
engineering_relevance: This suggests amino-silane surface treatments can directly lower interfacial losses in perovskite solar cells by stabilizing carrier landscapes at the nanoscale.
method: Amplitude-modulated Kelvin probe force microscopy (KPFM) on mixed-cation, mixed-halide perovskite thin films
Compare dark CPD and illuminated SPV before and after AEAPTMS passivation
Separate grain-boundary vs grain-interior surface potential contributions and assess wavelength-dependent SPV
evidence_signal: Passivation narrowed dark CPD distribution from about 45.7 to 14.6 mV, increased steady-state SPV from about 345 to 417 mV, and reduced the stabilization time constant from about 840 to 470 s.
watch_item: The results are based on thin-film nanoscale surface measurements, so translation to full device performance and long-term operational stability still needs verification.
paper_title: Understanding surface potential dynamics of passivated perovskites via Kelvin Probe Force Microscopy
